top_story: Iran’s 22 November strike on a Bahraini industrial facility, alongside hits on two tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, marks a sharp expansion of confrontation into Gulf infrastructure and shipping lanes, raising the risk that pressure on US military assets in Bahrain will spill directly onto civilian economies. This escalation compounds an older humanitarian collapse in Gaza, where displaced families were already entering another winter in exposed tent camps, showing how regional conflict is deepening civilian vulnerability on multiple fronts. In the occupied West Bank, the same day brought settler arson attacks on Palestinian villages and unusually blunt Israeli condemnation from senior political and military figures, exposing growing strain inside Israel over violence that is both politically destabilizing and socially radicalizing. The regional picture is one of widening insecurity in which state-to-state escalation, disrupted commerce, and unchecked communal attacks are reinforcing each other and narrowing space for civilian protection.
